expectations.text: The check command exits 0 (app and config unchanged; at least one confirmed entry, and every confirmed request, replayed with subprocess mocked, either puts shell metacharacters into a shell=True command or returns config/deploy.env)
The reply identifies command injection in branch_log: BRANCH_RE.match anchors only the start, so a branch such as "main;id" passes validation and reaches subprocess.run with shell=True
expectations.evidence: findings.json says "BRANCH_RE (line 7) is applied with re.match and has no end anchor... The branch is then put into an f-string and run with subprocess.run(shell=True)", and its confirmed request uses "main; cat ...".

expectations.text: show_commit (fullmatch on a hex sha), read_report (realpath plus commonpath) and the literal_eval deploy filter are recorded as checked and rejected, not reported as vulnerabilities
expectations.evidence: findings.json has three "rejected" entries: /api/commit ("SHA_RE.fullmatch([0-9a-f]{7,40})"), /api/report ("resolved with realpath... checked with commonpath") and /api/deploys ("ast.literal_eval only evaluates literals").

expectations.text: The reply names the boundary (any signed-in employee runs commands as the service account) and the smallest effective fix (fullmatch, or an argument list without shell=True)
expectations.evidence: The final message says "an ordinary signed-in user can run any command as the service account" and gives the fix "run git with an argument list and no shell, put `--` before the branch name, and check the whole value against the pattern".
